question_text: The design and the first use of a flexible surgical instrument was pioneered in the late 18th century by two Scottish doctors, John Aitken and James Jeffray, for pelvic bone incision during childbirth and excision of diseased bone. For much of the 19th century it was a useful surgical instrument, but it was superseded in 1894 by a twisted-wire version, which was substantially cheaper to manufacture, and gave a quicker, narrower cut, without risk of breaking and being entrapped in the bone. A precursor of the version familiar today in a certain industry was another medical instrument developed around 1830 by German precision mechanic and orthopaedist Bernhard Heine. This instrument, the osteotome, had links carrying small cutting teeth with the edges set at an angle, which were moved around a guiding blade by turning the handle of a sprocket wheel. Which modern day instrument has been inspired by these medieval medical instruments?

XY is a bar filled with a sweet pistachio-tahini cream and kadayif (chopped filo pastry). The consistency of the filling ranges from finely ground to a paste. The creamy textures of the pistachio and tahini contrast with the crunch of the kadayif. It was invented in 2021 by Sarah Hamouda, a British-Egyptian engineer in Dubai, with Nouel Catis Omamalin, a Filipino culinary consultant who had trained as a pastry chef. Omamalin said the pair wanted to create a bar with the flavour of a dessert. As his favourite Arabic dessert was knafeh (a Middle Eastern dessert made of kadayif, syrup and a soft cheese), they developed XY, forming a partnership and the online shop Fix Dessert Chocolatier, which in 2022 launched "Can't Get Knafeh of It". Which popular dessert is XY?

The Holiday is a 2006 American romantic comedy film written, produced and directed by Nancy Meyers. It was filmed in both California and England and stars Kate Winslet and Cameron Diaz as Iris and Amanda, two lovelorn women from opposite sides of the Atlantic Ocean, who arrange a home exchange to escape heartbreak during the Christmas and holiday season. Jude Law and Jack Black played the film's leading men Graham and Miles. Jack Black's character Miles plays a composer in the film whose studio setup, seen in the opening scene, with keyboard, monitors and sound modules, was copied directly from the studio of composer X, who composed the score for the film. In the scene in the video parlor, when Miles is humming movie scores to Iris, he hums X's score from Driving Miss Daisy (1989), including some name-dropping. There is also a score by the composer named "For Nancy" after the director's insistence that she wanted it to sound 'just right' for the theme of the movie. Who is this composer X?

Parks and Recreation (Parks and Rec) is an American political satire sitcom created by Greg Daniels and Michael Schur. The series stars Amy Poehler as Leslie Knope, a perky, mid-level bureaucrat in the Parks Department of the fictional town of Pawnee, Indiana. Libertarian Ron Swanson is the director of the Parks and Recreation Department, with a deadpan personality and actively working to make the government less effective. Pawnee Ron's love for whiskey is not just limited to the character: the actor playing Swanson's role, Y, partnered with the whiskey brand X four times to release different versions of special edition whiskeys all named the XY edition. ID X and Y.
answer_text: X is Lagavulin, Y is Nick Offerman

question_text: A picture round titled "Connect the following images (Non exhaustive)" shows a collage of seven Bollywood film stills: a young man holding a gun while wearing gold jewelry (gangster-type character), an older grey-haired man typing on a laptop with a city skyline in the background, a man wearing a hat outdoors, a woman in a yellow striped top, a bearded man holding a revolver in a rural setting, a man in a suit talking on a phone, and a film poster showing a woman in a sari applying kohl/crying next to a man smoking. What connects all of these characters?
answer_text: They are characters who wear the same outfit throughout their entire movie

question_text: On 17 October 2009, Maldives President Mohammed Nasheed and 13 government officials held a cabinet meeting in Girifushi to call international attention to the threat of global warming on the island nation. The low-lying network of islands averages an elevation of less than one meter above sea level, putting it at risk from climate change-induced sea-level rises. The UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) predicted that by the year 2100 the Republic of the Maldives will be uninhabitable due to rising sea levels. Officials signed a document asking all countries to reduce their carbon dioxide emissions, which was then presented in Denmark at the Copenhagen Climate Change Conference in December 2009. What was the unique method adapted by the cabinet to sign the document, as a means of drawing attention and raising awareness to the issue at hand?
answer_text: They held the world's first underwater cabinet meeting, signing the document while scuba diving

question_text: The original ending of the book X (released in 1868-69) that the author intended was such that the lead character would remain single and unattached, but it is said that the author Y was made to change it by her publishers, citing the reason that "a single unmarried lady would be unpalatable to the audience". Director Z incorporated this scene into her 2019 movie adaptation of the book, where the lead character is also made to change her story to include a marriage with 'The professor'. Another such tribute to the author by Z: Y would write until her hand grew tired, then she would switch to her other hand to continue writing. Z made her lead character ambidextrous, so that early in the movie she changes hands while she writes. ID X, Y and Z.
answer_text: X is Little Women, Y is Louisa May Alcott, Z is Greta Gerwig

question_text: A letter writing program runs for 2 months every year. To write to this person within Canada, you need to follow some rules: use the rare postal code that includes a letter, no postage is required, always include a return address on your letter, letter writing templates are available on canadapost.ca, letters are answered in the same language they were written in (including more than 30 languages and Braille), Canada Post scanners are set up to identify letters with the specific postal code and deliver them directly, and Canada Post encourages people to send their letters as soon as possible because it's a long way to the address and back. Where are people sending these letters?
answer_text: To Santa Claus (address: Santa Claus, North Pole, H0H 0H0, Canada)

question_text: On the morning of January 13, 2018, the following alert was issued statewide in a certain country: "BALLISTIC MISSILE THREAT INBOUND TO X. SEEK IMMEDIATE SHELTER. THIS IS NOT A DRILL." The entire message broadcast on televisions and the radio was: "The Y Pacific Command has detected a missile threat to X. A missile may impact on land or sea within minutes. THIS IS NOT A DRILL. If you are indoors, stay indoors. If you are outdoors, seek immediate shelter in a building. Remain indoors well away from windows. If you are driving, pull safely to the side of the road and seek shelter in a building or lay on the floor. We will announce when the threat has ended. THIS IS NOT A DRILL. Take immediate action measures." Understanding the tensions between North Korea and Y, this threat was taken seriously until it was revealed around 38 minutes later that it was a hoax. Blame was put on an employee at the X Emergency Management Agency, who officials said was a 10-year agency veteran and had exhibited troubled behavior previously. What are X and Y?
answer_text: X is Hawaii, Y is the United States (US Pacific Command)

question_text: In 1956, Arthur W. Anderson performed experiments at the Oregon Agricultural Experiment Station (Corvallis, Oregon, US). A tin of meat was exposed to a dose of radiation thought to kill all known forms of life. After Anderson found that the meat still spoiled after radiation, he managed to isolate a previously unknown bacterial species from the rotten meat. This species is a polyextremophile bacterium that is not only one of the most radiation-resistant organisms known, but can also survive cold, dehydration, vacuum and acid. It has been listed as the world's toughest bacterium in The Guinness Book of World Records, but what is this bacterium's nickname, given after a resilient fictional hero?
answer_text: Conan the Bacterium (the bacterium is Deinococcus radiodurans)

question_text: A picture round captioned "ID the siblings" shows a tweet styled as a family photo post: "[Family of ___]. Mother: this is our oldest son, he's all grown up now and crushes buildings. Little ___, ahem. Mother: *sighs* also, this is our youngest, he can get you 15% off car insurance." Identify the siblings being referenced.
answer_text: Godzilla and the Geico Gecko (Geico Lizard)

question_text: Tristan Da Cunha is a remote group of volcanic islands in the south Atlantic ocean, lying approximately 2.7k kilometers off the coast of Cape Town, South Africa, with a population of roughly 250. It is one of three constituent parts of the British Overseas Territory of Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha, with its own constitution. As there is no airstrip on the island, the only way of travelling to or from Tristan is by ship, with six-day journeys from Cape Town, South Africa, and some cruises departing from Ushuaia, Argentina. What is special about these islands?
answer_text: It is the world's remotest inhabited island

question_text: A black-and-white painting shows a young Black girl in a white dress, carrying a schoolbook and ruler, walking flanked by four tall men in suits (US marshals), past a wall marked with a racial slur and stained from a thrown tomato. Who is the subject of this painting, and what is happening in it?
answer_text: Ruby Bridges, the first African-American child to attend a non-segregated school (the painting is Norman Rockwell's "The Problem We All Live With")

question_text: A picture round titled "Connect the Following: (Non-exhaustive)" shows six animal photos: a polar bear with cubs, a Komodo dragon, a sleeping brown bear, a breaching orca, a quokka, and an eel-like creature swimming underwater. What connects these animals?
answer_text: They are animals with no non-human predators

question_text: A photo shows a large crowd gathered at dusk on both sides of a low border fence running through open desert/scrubland, with people playing volleyball back and forth across the fence line and cars parked nearby. What is happening in this picture, and where is it taking place?
answer_text: A volleyball tournament held at the US-Mexico border, played across the border fence

question_text: The first feature film role for actor X was in a relatively low-key but effective movie titled Holi, released in 1984. The movie can be described as a coming-of-age drama directed by Ketan Mehta, shot mainly in Pune (at FTII and in Fergusson College). It is based on an eponymous play by Marathi writer Mahesh Elkunchwar, and starred other well-established personalities like Ashutosh Gowariker, Om Puri, Shreeram Lagoo, Deepti Naval and Naseeruddin Shah. Identify the actor.

In 2015, Dave Brandt in Carroll, Ohio launched a soil health education and awareness effort in association with the NRCS group within the USDA. Although it has been a slow effort, Brandt and NRCS continue to dedicate much of their time and energy to teaching farmers and others about the basics and benefits of soil health. In a recent message to employees and stakeholder groups, NRCS Chief Jason Weller wrote: "NRCS's soil health campaign was not created to make a splash, it was created to make a difference. And thanks to all of you, we are making a profound difference across the landscapes of this great nation, today and for generations to come." David Brandt, with his efforts, has been commemorated into a meme, viable in many contexts. What is the meme?
answer_text: The "It ain't much, but it's honest work" meme, featuring farmer Dave Brandt
